_comment: Workflow control parameters for the Millennium copy. The orchestrator is a DEVELOPMENT TOOL for architecture/dev/review/investigation loops; it is not the runtime foundation of the travel agent product. Config is authoritative for agent<->role binding and limits; the engine owns control flow. Paths are resolved relative to the orchestration/ directory.

paths._comment: repo_root is the Millennium workspace root and the cwd every agent CLI is launched in. dev_repos are development targets the Developer MAY edit; analysis_repos are read-only context. The current workspace root is not yet a git repo, so real runs require either making the target a git repo or passing --allow-unguarded knowingly. Mock runs always work.

guard._comment: exclude_prefix is applied within each watched repo; the orchestration/ tool dir lives at the workspace root (outside every watched repo), so its run output never appears in any repo's status.

validation._comment: RESERVED / NOT YET ENFORCED. The orchestrator itself never executes build/test commands; the Developer (Claude) agent runs them inside its own sandbox during its step. These fields document intended policy and are read by no code today: reviewers stay pure-analysis. Wiring orchestrator-side command execution is deliberately out of scope for the conservative first cut.

architecture._comment: Developer-centric chain, two escalation tiers. Codex (System Architect) AUTHORS the proposal; the MAX-EFFORT Claude Developer Verifier is the PRIMARY reviewer — the developer who will build it does the developer review of every draft (FEASIBLE/NEEDS_REVISION/HUMAN_REQUIRED) and FEASIBLE is required but NOT sufficient: after the Developer returns FEASIBLE the Tech Lead runs a MANDATORY control review and its READY_FOR_HUMAN_REVIEW is the PASS (a control rejection sends the Architect back to revise + the Developer to re-verify). An Architect<->Developer deadlock (never FEASIBLE) routes to Tech-Lead arbitration (tier 1); a Tech-Lead control/arbitration deadlock or ESCALATE routes to the Arbiter (tier 2). No standalone code-review gate. (Tech-Lead control gate added 2026-06-19, Irina.) Agents are resolved by `roster` at run start (the per-cell `agent` below is the all-live default and is overwritten by the roster). (Restructured 2026-06-15; roster 2026-06-15.)

roster._comment: Approved chain (Irina 2026-06-15): codex · opus(pinned dev, max-effort) · gemini · deepseek · sonnet · haiku. developer_verifier is PINNED to claude_reviewer — the shift-left jumps OVER it so the developer review is ALWAYS a real Claude developer, never displaced to another vendor (if opus itself exhausts the pin falls back to claude_sonnet→claude_haiku, still Claude). Non-pinned cells (author, tech_lead, arbiter) fill positionally from the live chain. With codex disabled: author=gemini, dev_verifier=claude_reviewer, tech_lead=deepseek, arbiter=claude_sonnet.

development._comment: Claude (Responsible Developer) implements; CODE review is by a MAX-EFFORT Claude too (Software Engineering Code Reviewer, ultrathink) — developers peer-review each other's code, as in real life, and the reviewer runs at max thinking budget to offset the shared-blind-spot risk of same-model review. Codex does the ARCHITECTURE review (System Architect). STAGED gate (Irina 2026-06-22): code-review runs FIRST; only when it PASSES does the Architect review; only when the Architect passes does the Tech Lead (final gate) run. An architecture question raised mid-implementation is answered by the ARCHITECT, not the arbiter; the Arbiter is called ONLY to break a genuine deadlock (the same blocker repeats > trigger_after_cycles). Agents resolved by `roster` at run start. (staged gate + arbiter-on-deadlock 2026-06-22; roster 2026-06-15.)

roster._comment: Approved chain (Irina 2026-06-15): opus · opus(max-effort reviewer) · codex · gemini · deepseek · sonnet · haiku. cell[i]=chain[i] when all live; an unavailable/disabled/EXHAUSTED agent shifts the chain left. With codex disabled: developer=claude, code_reviewer=claude_reviewer, architect=gemini, tech_lead=deepseek, arbiter=claude_sonnet.

investigation._comment: Root-cause investigation loop. Investigator (Claude/Opus) reads the task-named files/repos/logs/contracts, correlates evidence, and proposes falsifiable hypotheses; it is the ONLY role that may edit/build, and only in dev_repos. Refuter attacks every cycle until it cannot break a hypothesis; the independent Verifier is then the final gate, attacking from a fresh angle; the Arbiter is invoked only on escalation/deadlock. Agents resolved by `roster` at run start. Ends ROOT_CAUSE_ESTABLISHED / NO_DEFECT_FOUND (success) or HUMAN_REQUIRED.
investigation._max_iterations_note: Lowered 10->5 on 2026-06-16: a round-9 run thrashed for 6+ iterations (investigator kept re-deriving, refuter kept refuting) without converging. A focused, code-anchored task should converge in 2-3; 5 is a guardrail against burning hours + DeepSeek balance on non-convergence.

roster._comment: Approved chain (Irina 2026-06-15): opus · codex · gemini · deepseek · sonnet · haiku. cell[i]=chain[i] when all live; an unavailable/disabled/EXHAUSTED agent shifts the chain left. The judge (arbiter) is filled positionally, NOT reserved from the strong end. With codex disabled: investigator=claude(opus), refuter=gemini, verifier=deepseek, arbiter=claude_sonnet.
